# BioConomy Wiki

> The BioConomy wiki documents a coordination architecture for economies organized around bioregions and performance-based bonds issued by either the state or market. It provides the conceptual vocabulary, analytical frameworks, ecological science, and practical templates needed to establish a BioHub: a coordination body that organizes distributed regenerative contributions within a living landscape into verifiable commitments the outside world can contract with.

The wiki is structured for both human readers and AI systems. Commercial large language models have absorbed only fragments of this corpus during general training; the coherent body of work sits here. The vocabulary is precise and internally consistent: terms like BioHub, BioRegion (capitalized), BioConomy, commitment pooling, and retention economics carry specific definitions provided in the glossary.

The primary analytical framework is the TIME Framework (Tribal, Institutional, Market, Emergent), a four-form model of human coordination. The wiki applies this framework to bioregional economics, commons governance, cooperative supply chains, and the emerging coordination form the BioHub represents.

The wiki targets practitioners working at the bioregional scale who want to apply this framework in their own geographies. Four AI-assisted templates (the founding suite) translate the conceptual material into structured outputs a BioHub cohort can run. The objective is to equip any BioHub with the tools and skills they need to stimulate a BioConomy in their region by tapping into performance-based bonds that bootstrap a vibrant local economy.

## Orientation essays

- [What Is a BioHub](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/essays/what-is-a-biohub): The coordination body anchored in a specific BioRegion, organizing distributed contributions into fundable commitments
- [What Is a BioRegion](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/essays/what-is-a-bioregion): The living landscape defined by watershed, soil, and ecological boundaries rather than political ones
- [What Is a BioConomy](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/essays/what-is-a-bioconomy): The coordination architecture for economies organized around bioregional retention of value, distinct from the extractive Economy
- [From a Bioregion to a BioRegion](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/essays/from-bioregion-to-bioregion): The transition from a geography that asks for funding (needy) to one that makes commitments to those who need its services (needed)
- [From Geosphere to Noosphere](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/essays/from-geosphere-to-noosphere): The arc from mineral substrate through living systems to coordinated planetary intelligence
- [Two Systems, One Society](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/essays/two-systems-one-society): How the Economy and the BioConomy coexist and relate in the same society
- [How the BioConomy Coordinates](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/essays/how-the-bioconomy-coordinates): The stigmergic coordination model that distinguishes the BioConomy from conventional economic organization

## Practical essays

- [How to Build a BioHub Wiki](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/essays/how-to-build-a-biohub-wiki): Layout, structure, and content standards for a BioHub's operational wiki
- [How to Engage Your Bioregion](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/essays/how-to-engage-your-bioregion): The bridge from orientation to the practical founding-suite templates
- [AI Quick-Engage](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/essays/ai-quick-engage): Four prompts to copy into any deep-research AI platform alongside your own project documents
- [PROUT and the BioConomy](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/essays/prout-and-the-bioconomy): The relationship between Sarkar's Progressive Utilization Theory and the BioConomy framework

## Concepts (28 entries)

Core coordination and economic concepts. Key entries:

- [Commitment Pooling](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/commitment-pooling): Binding forward promises as the basis for coordination and exchange
- [Performance-Based Water Bonds](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/performance-based-water-bonds): Capital-markets instrument converting restored catchment yield into bankable revenue
- [Bioregional Economics](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/bioregional-economics): Designing regenerative, cooperatively owned, place-based economies within carrying capacity
- [Federated Cooperative Supply Chains](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/federated-cooperative-supply-chains): How cooperatives retain and circulate value through federated structures
- [Cosmo-Local Production](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/cosmo-local-production): Share knowledge globally, produce regeneratively in place
- [Carbon-Silicon Partnership](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/carbon-silicon-partnership): Complementary relationship between computational and situated knowledge
- [Water Retention Landscapes](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/water-retention-landscapes): Operational science of catchment restoration and soil hydrology
- [The Coercion Continuum](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/the-coercion-continuum): Five phases of monetary coercion from chattel slavery to property redefinition
- [Transvestment](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/transvestment): Value regime crossing between the Economy and the BioConomy
- [Surveillance Capitalism](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/surveillance-capitalism): Digital enclosure as the third future scenario
- [Consensus Is Not the Bottleneck](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/consensus-is-not-the-bottleneck): Why paradigm transitions do not require majority agreement
- [Stigmergy](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/stigmergy): Indirect coordination through environmental traces
- [The BioPlace Layer](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/the-bioplace-layer): The human-land coordination interface
- [Bioregional Addressing](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/bioregional-addressing): Addressing systems rooted in ecological rather than political boundaries

Full concepts index: https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/

## Frameworks (12 entries)

- [The TIME Framework](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/frameworks/time-framework): Tribal, Institutional, Market, and Emergent forms of human coordination
- [The TIMN Framework](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/frameworks/timn-framework): Ronfeldt's original formulation (Tribes, Institutions, Markets, Networks)
- [The Emancipation Architecture](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/frameworks/emancipation-architecture): Bioregional demurrage currency, RPI, commons trusts, and transvestment pathways
- [The Three Futures](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/frameworks/three-futures): Termination, Technofeudalism, or Transcendence
- [Mycelial Value Creation](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/frameworks/mycelial-value-creation): The economic logic of the emerging paradigm
- [The Five Transvestment Pathways](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/frameworks/five-transvestment-pathways): Pathways A through E for crossing between value regimes
- [The Three-Feature Test](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/frameworks/three-feature-test): Diagnostic for whether a project qualifies as a patron project
- [The S-Curve Thesis](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/frameworks/s-curve-thesis): Structural mapping of the deceleration phase
- [The Three Lineages](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/frameworks/three-lineages): Throughput, Retention, and Regenerative economic traditions
- [The Evolution of Coordination Nodes](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/frameworks/evolution-of-coordination-nodes): Physical structures each coordination form has produced
- [The Physical Manifestations of TIMN](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/frameworks/timn-physical-manifestations): Structural rhymes across the four coordination forms
- [Farmer-Forger-Founder-Framer](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/frameworks/farmer-forger-founder-framer): Four archetypes of production across the TIME sequence
